edit.description: `source_deps` and `source_dep_stale` each own a read-and-parse-and-increment body over the very file `read_lock_document` already opens, and both diverge from it exactly the way the emit-side body did before d48ce8c7: on a missing lock they return early counting neither read nor parse, where the door counts one of each. Both fold to one line through the door (`source_deps_from_doc(&read_lock_document(workspace_dir)?, family_key)`, and the same for the stale body), which moves the six public faces they back — `layout_imports`, `includes`, `inputs`, `layout_import_stale`, `include_stale`, `input_stale` — from `Result<_, DriftError>` to `miette::Result<_>`, the shape the two already-folded siblings `layout_prose` and `layout_sources` already wear. The `*_from_doc` faces are untouched: they are what `src/gate.rs` calls, so no production count moves. Census by behavior, not by helper name (`rg 'crate::LOCK_FILENAME' src/`): every other site is a path join or an `is_file` probe (`src/gate.rs`, `src/main.rs`, `src/install.rs`, `src/import.rs`, `src/compose.rs`), except `read_layer_clauses` in `src/compose.rs`, which reads a *different* lock — a `--layer` argument's, fail-closed on absence where the host read tolerates it, as its own doc states — and drift.rs's `every_root_key_is_reserved` unit test, which reads the raw bytes on purpose to judge what the writer wrote. After the fold the door is the only body that reads the host lock. Rejected alternative, named per the section: delete the six path-taking faces and spell `*_from_doc(&read_lock_document(dir).unwrap())` at their test call sites — it removes more surface, but fans out to four test files for no behavioral gain and leaves `layout_prose`/`layout_sources` an inconsistent remainder; extending the existing surface beats deleting a face the test suite legitimately consumes.

The pin that would have caught it, beside `emit_over_a_lockless_harness_reads_and_parses_once` and built the same way: over a harness whose `.temper/` carries no lock (asserted absent, so the pin cannot go vacuous), one call to `drift::includes` and one to `drift::include_stale` each move `lock_read_count`/`lock_parse_count` by one — 0/0 on the pre-fold tree, 1/1 with the fold.

summary: The host lock's last two hand-rolled read-and-parse bodies fold into the counted door, so a source-dep face costs the same count as every other lock face.

tests.asserts: a source-dep face and a source-dep stale face over a lockless harness each read and parse the lock exactly once, the count the counted door already charged every other face

acceptance: cargo test green with the new lockless pin, and cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings clean over the six re-typed faces' call sites.
notes: The six faces have no engine caller — `src/gate.rs` takes the `*_from_doc` side — so today's divergence is latent rather than a live miscount, which is why this is the residue class and not a bug report. No test couples to a `DriftError` variant from any of the six (`lock_declaration_rows.rs` does `.unwrap_err()` on `layout_sources`, already miette), so the return-type move is free at the call sites. scoped at 040e2d1c
